newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 27.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Swedish and South African security authorities are to investigate allegations of an official apartheid government link to Swedish Prime Minister Olof Palme's assassination in 1986.
- The Development Bank of Southern Africa has axed 55 of its 75 senior management posts in a major restructuring of its business.

- Nissan South Africa plans to retrench close to 20 percent of its workforce within the next two months if negotiations with the National Union of Metalworkers fail to produce alternative ways to cut costs.
- The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission will issue an opinion in the next few weeks on the legality of the asset swaps South Africa has permitted since the beginning of the year.
- South Africa's trade unions are displaying a new-found realism by moderating their demands and accepting smaller wage increases, according to labour consultants Andrew Levy and Associates.
- Swedish police confirm name of South African spy Craig Williamson featured in their investigation into 1986 murder of Prime Minister Olof Palme.
- Police and soldiers patrol Buffelsfontein mine near Klerksdorp, scene of ethnic fighting in which more than 20 miners have been killed since Saturday midnight.
- Remains of at least one body are found buried in concrete in two drums on a rubbish dump in Lenasia outside Johannesburg.

- Potential clash between the Truth and Reconciliation Commission and the defence force is averted after talks between Deputy Defence Minister Ronnie Kasrils and commission deputy chairman Alex Boraine.
